claims.claim: Perception is the process of organizing and interpreting sensory information into meaningful experience.
Sensation is the raw detection of physical energy by sensory receptors; perception is the meaning built from that input, and the two are distinct stages.

Bottom-up processing is data-driven: incoming stimulus information initiates and determines higher-level recognition; top-down processing is knowledge-driven: higher-level knowledge, concepts, and expectations influence how incoming data are interpreted.

The Gestalt psychologists (notably Max Wertheimer, Wolfgang Köhler, and Kurt Koffka) held that perception organizes sensory elements into wholes that are more than the sum of their parts, and they derived principles describing how the brain does this in predictable ways.
The figure-ground principle: perception divides a visual scene into a figure that stands out and a ground behind it, and the same input can support different figure-ground splits.

The laws of grouping: the brain clusters separate elements into unified groups by rules such as proximity (closeness) and similarity (likeness); the laws of grouping were identified by Max Wertheimer in 1923.
Expectations and context shape perception: a perceptual set is a temporary readiness to perceive certain objects or events rather than others, informed by expectations, experience, and context.

Perception is constructive, not camera-like: perceptions rest on perceptual hypotheses — educated guesses informed by personalities, experiences, and expectations — so perception can differ between people and can be wrong.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Definitional wording of perception differs slightly across authoritative sources.
positions: APA Dictionary of Psychology: perception is the process or result of becoming aware of objects, relationships, and events by means of the senses; these activities enable organisms to organize and interpret the stimuli received into meaningful knowledge.
OpenStax Psychology 2e: perception refers to the way sensory information is organized, interpreted, and consciously experienced.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The two formulations agree on the core — organizing and interpreting sensory input — so the lesson uses that shared core as the working definition and attributes it to both sources.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Scope of the figure-ground assumption has been questioned in the research literature.
positions: OpenStax Psychology 2e notes that the assumption that the ability to interpret sensory information depends on what is labeled figure versus ground has been called into question (Peterson & Gibson, 1994; Vecera & O'Reilly, 1998).
Standard textbook treatment presents figure-ground as a core, well-established Gestalt principle of organization.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson presents figure-ground as a widely taught organizing principle of perception without claiming it explains every aspect of visual interpretation; the working example is presented as an illustration of the principle, not as a universal law.

sourceRecords.title: Sensation — APA Dictionary of Psychology
sourceRecords.notes: Definition read via the APA Dictionary public JSON API on 2026-08-22. Supports sensation as the process or experience of perceiving through the senses and as an irreducible unit of experience produced by stimulation of a sensory receptor. Used as reference for the sensation side of the sensation-perception distinction.

sourceRecords.title: Bottom-up processing — APA Dictionary of Psychology
sourceRecords.notes: Definition read via the APA Dictionary public JSON API on 2026-08-22. Supports bottom-up processing as data-driven processing in which incoming stimulus data initiate and determine higher-level recognition, typically used when information is unfamiliar. The lesson's thixotropy example is original.

sourceRecords.title: Top-down processing — APA Dictionary of Psychology
sourceRecords.notes: Definition read via the APA Dictionary public JSON API on 2026-08-22. Supports top-down processing as conceptually driven processing in which higher-level knowledge, concepts, or expectations influence the processing of lower-level information; the APA's own example concerns reading. The lesson's parking-garage EXIT sign example is original.

sourceRecords.title: Figure–ground — APA Dictionary of Psychology
sourceRecords.notes: Definition read via the APA Dictionary public JSON API on 2026-08-22. Supports the figure-ground principle: perceptions have two parts — a figure or object that stands out in good contour and an indistinct, homogeneous background. The lesson's doorway/pale-wall example is original.

sourceRecords.title: Gestalt principles of organization — APA Dictionary of Psychology
sourceRecords.notes: Definition read via the APA Dictionary public JSON API on 2026-08-22. Supports: principles derived by the Gestalt psychologists; tendency to perceive configurations at the level of the whole rather than component features; laws of grouping identified by German psychologist Max Wertheimer in 1923 (closure, common fate, good continuation, proximity, similarity, symmetry).

sourceRecords.title: Perceptual set — APA Dictionary of Psychology
sourceRecords.notes: Definition read via the APA Dictionary public JSON API on 2026-08-22. Supports perceptual set as a temporary readiness to perceive certain objects or events rather than others, and as a schema or frame that influences perception. The lesson's delivery-van example is original.
